To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bacterial community structure of an aquifer was affected by grazing but not by changes in acetat
the addition of carbon and the removal of predators affected bacterial communities in groundwater.

(a) the bacterial community composition was affected by grazing mortality and was not influenced by changes in substrate availability and (b) acetate assimilation and/or metabolization were used as a proxy to distinguish active and inactive bacterial cells in the groundwater.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of protozoan grazing and the availability of carbon sources on bacterial community structure in a groundwater aquifer.
the effect of predation and substrate supply on the structure of the microbial community in groundwater.
the effect of predation on the bacterial community structure in the presence and absence of carbon substrate in groundwater.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of carbon and predation had no effect on the acetate-assimilation bacterial population in groundwater.
the bacterial community in groundwater was not affected by the addition of acetate, but the protozoan population had a significant impact.
the protozoan grazes are the major controlling factors in determining the bacterial community in the subsurface.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
protozoans play a major role in structuring the bacterial community in the subsurface environment.
the bacterial community structure in a groundwater system is not affected by the availability of organic carbon but is affected by protozoan grazing.
acetate assimilation is not the main mechanism that shapes the bacterial community composition in groundwater.
The main takeaway from our work is that
grazing pressure, not organic carbon availability, is a major factor in shaping the groundwater bacterial community.
grazing by protozoan predators is an important factor in shaping the bacterial community composition in the aquifer.
the microbial community in the subsurface is shaped more by grazing pressure than by carbon availability.
